title: Amigurumi butterfly
excerpt: A colourful butterfly with a slim oval body and four oval wings. The wings are worked flat with no wire support; shaping comes from blocking and a central pinch seam. INTERMEDIATE due to multi-piece assembly. Approx 12 cm wingspan.
sourceNotes: Wire-free amigurumi butterfly wings are achieved through flat oval construction and blocking; techniques synthesised from common amigurumi practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: An oval piece worked flat by turning the work at the end of each row rather than working in continuous rounds. Working flat produces a piece with two smooth faces and a neat edge, which sits naturally as a wing when attached to the body. The oval is not stuffed.

A small gather sewn across the inner edge of each wing before attachment. Pinching about 1 cm of the straight edge and stitching it flat creates a slight cup that gives the wing a natural angled lift without wire or stiffener.

Dampening the finished flat pieces and pinning them to shape while damp. For these wings, blocking spreads the oval into a broader, thinner shape and dries with a slight stiffness that holds the wing outline. No starch or stiffener is needed with most dk yarns.

crochet.gaugeText: 24 dc × 28 rows = 10 × 10 cm in dk yarn on a 3.5 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx 12 cm wingspan x 8 cm tall.

content.text: Work the body as a slim oval. Work all four wings as
flat oval wings
, turning each row. Block wings after completion using
wet blocking
, pinning to the finished shape.
Body (8 rounds): 2.5 cm slim oval.
Upper wings (make 2, 11 rounds each): 3.5 cm oval, worked flat.
Lower wings (make 2, 8 rounds each): 2.5 cm oval, worked flat.
Wings
Work each upper and lower wing flat. Apply
wet blocking
and pin to shape. Once dry, work a
pinch seam
across the inner 1 cm of each wing edge.
Colour work
Work wings in your chosen butterfly colours. Surface embroider wing markings with a contrasting colour after blocking.
Assembly
Attach upper wings to the top third of the body and lower wings to the middle third. Angle upper wings upward and lower wings outward. Embroider antennae in black, knotting each tip.
What to try next
The dragonfly uses a long capsule body and four narrow wings in the same flat oval technique.
